review_notes: No eligible baseline regression is reported. The paper identifies its central question as estimating a dynamic model of manipulation (physical p. 2), classifies its approach as structural estimation (physical p. 9), and states that the main model is estimated using simulated method of moments (SMM) (physical pp. 3, 21). Section 5.1 says most parameters are estimated by SMM or measured from data, then specifies six structural parameters estimated by SMM (physical p. 21). Table 4, the primary-results table, is titled “Structural parameter estimates” and reports a test of overidentifying restrictions (physical p. 53). These are structural parameter estimates from an SMM fit, not observed-variable regression coefficients. Table 1 describes the earnings-response coefficient as a data input estimated using three-year rolling-window regressions within industry-year partitions (physical p. 50); that construction regression is not the paper’s principal empirical family, and no retained baseline regression depends on it. The displayed restrictions and optimal-bias relations in the identification discussion are structural moment conditions, not regression equations. Therefore the specification has models=[] and status=no_baseline_regression.

Checked source quotations (literal text, one page each): p.2: “This paper quantifies the incidence and magnitude of undetected misstatements by estimating a dynamic model of manipulation.” p.3: “I estimate the model using the simulated method of moments (SMM)” p.9: “Methodologically, this paper belongs to the structural estimation literature.” p.21: “Most of the model parameters are estimated using the simulated method of moments (SMM) or are measured from the data.” p.21: “then estimate the following six parameters using SMM” p.50: “three-year rolling-window regressions of price on income before extraordinary” p.50: “per share within industry-year partitions” p.53: “Structural parameter estimates” p.53: “overidentifying restrictions”
